findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the designated handwashing sink in the bar area was being used as a dump sink, despite facility procedure to use a separate bucket for waste bar liquids. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and educated staff about only using the handwashing sink for handwashing, and that the separate bucket should be used for waste bar liquids. An additional sign was placed above the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for any other purposes other than handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that a container of sausage gravy in the bottom part of the main prep cooler was measured at an internal temperature of 60 F. PIC stated that the sausage gravy had been recently put back in the cooler 30 minutes previously after being out for part of service. Inspector checked the internal temperature again 30 minutes later and the gravy was at 62 F. Inspector observes that all other items in the cooler are sufficiently cold holding at 41 F and below, and that the cooler has an ambient air temperature of 36 F. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the sausage gravy. Inspector and PIC discussed storing the sausage gravy, and other items that get cooled, in shallower pans so as to allow for more rapid cooling, and making sure staff are more aware of how long items are left on the counter. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F or less, and that items can cool quickly once placed in cold holding equipment.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the kitchen triple sink and the bar sanitizer bucket to be held at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- sanitizer tablets were added and observed to be changed to 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizers are made and tested at a frequency to hold the sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed that the sliding cooler in the storage room to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed an ambient thermometer in the cooler.Ensure all cooling units holding temperature control for food safety (TCS) contain an ambient thermometer to monitor air temperatures at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a wet mop head stored in the basin of a mop bucket. The PIC was informed and will be reminding staff of appropriate mop storage. Ensure wet mops are placed in a position that allows for air drying to prevent the harborage of microorganisms with a high water activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple cans (sliced stew tomatoes X5, pineapple chunks X1, and black olives X1) in dry storage to contain dents along the seams, or significant dents along the body. CORRECTED- inspectors discussed can denting and Botulism entry with the kitchen staff and person in charge (PIC). Regularly check for dents along the seams of cans, and for large dents throughout the body. Ensure dented cans are marked or separated from cans for service to be returned to food supplier.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed soda nozzles at the server station (Dr. Pepper, Diet Coke, Coke, and Mellow Yellow) to contain an accumulation of soil debris and a biofilm. CORRECTED- the soda nozzles were removed, and brought to the bar triple sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The PIC found extra nozzles to switch out the current nozzles, for more frequent cleaning. Inspector and PIC discussed verifying cleaning methods for Coke equipment with supplier. These surfaces are considered food contact surfaces and could serve as a source of contamination.  Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of biofilms and soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors two opened containers of milk (2% in the kitchen cooler and chocolate at the bar) lacking date marking. Inspectors asked the PIC when the milks were opened. CORRECTED- the PIC was able to remember when the chocolate milk was opened and put the corresponding date on the container. PIC was unable to verify when the 2% was opened, and the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no consumer advisory in the menu. A discussion occurred with the person in charge (PIC), and while most burgers are fully cooked, some customers do request to have their hamburgers not fully cooked. Inspector left consumer advisory guidelines with the PIC. The next time the menu is printed the facility must include a disclosure (using words such as “raw” or undercooked”, or an asterisk that leads to the reminder), and a reminder regarding the increased risk of food-borne illness associated with consuming undercooked animal proteins. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(C) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (C) REMINDER shall include asterisking the animal-derived FOODS requiring DISCLOSURE to a footnote that states: (1) Regarding the safety of these items, written information is available upon request; (2) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness; or (3) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. [C]

NOTE: Close the lids on the top holding area for prep coolers during slow periods to help maintain colder temperatures. Also be mindful on how product is stacked in containers and avoid over filling.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open package of deli turkey was observed without a date mark in the bottom of the small prep cooler. Product was opened over the weekend. Turkey was dated and kept for use. 
--Slaw in the 3 door cooler was without a date mark. Cook stated the product was made the previous Friday. Slaw was dated and kept for use.
--Cooked sausage was observed in the 3 door cooler with a prep date of 2/17 and use by date of 2/24. Use by date was 2/23 the day prior. Sausage was discarded.
--White gravy was observed in the 3 door cooler with a prep date of 2/10 and was well past the 7 day time frame for use. Gravy was discarded. 
--Baked beans and cheese sauce were in containers with dates that were not legible in the 3 door cooler. Cook was unsure as to the prep date and discarded both items.
NOTE: Make sure foods are properly dated with labels that are easy to read.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Mushrooms were sliced and added to vegetable mix cooking on the grill without first washing. Package label stated to wash before use. Ensure proper washing of all unwashed produce prior to use.
Raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed in water to remove soil and other contaminants before being cut, combined with other ingredients, cooked, served, or offered for human consumption in reacy-to-eat form

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-202.11 Light bulbs in back prep area of kitchen and in the dry storage room were missing covers. Manger thought they were coated and possibly shatter resistant, but it was not apparent at the time of inspection (packaging unavailable). Ensure information is maintained if light bulbs are coated and shatter resistant, which negates the need for light shields. Otherwise, provide light shields on the fixtures. 
Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Bar manager was observed handling sliced lemon for a drink garnish with bare hands. Use of tongs, gloves, or another acceptable method (toothpicks, etc.) for handling drink garnishes was discussed. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Chunks of ice were observed in the drain of the kitchen handsink indicating it was used as a dump sink at some point. All staff were advised on proper use of handsinks for handwashing only. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Do not use handsinks as dump sinks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Gray digital stem thermometer used for checking food temperatures was soiled with grease and food debris in storage jar. Cook was advised on proper use and cleaning/sanitizing of food thermometers between uses. Stems of food thermometers were cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Sausage gravy prepared for breakfast service was observed with surface and internal temperature at 66F and 80F respectively. Cook on duty did not work the morning shift and was unsure as to the exact time the gravy was cooked and/or when the cooling process began. Time was not indicated on the label. Gravy was discarded. Tracking of time and temperature to ensure proper cooling was discussed - consider using the dry erase board to write the time/temperature and track the cooling process so there is no confusion on time frame and/or if products are cooling properly, especially between shift changes. 
Cooked TCS food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 A metal stem thermometer available for use in the kitchen was observed reading at 0F at ambient temperature. Cook stated a gray digital stem thermometer is the one typically used, and that thermometer was reading around 74F at ambient temperature. One other digital thermometer didn't turn on and likely needed a battery. Cook was advised to ensure proper calibration and function of thermometers available for use. Metal stem thermometer and digital thermometer were calibrated during the inspection. 
Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
NOTE: Food thermometers need to be calibrated frequently to ensure accuracy while monitoring food temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Manager began to eat a hard boiled egg over the large prep table while discussing prep time and temperature of said food item. Manger immediately left the kitchen upon request of inspector. 
Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee was observed washing hands at the kitchen 3 part sink. Employee was advised to wash hands at the handsink and went to the designated handsink to finish handwashing. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda gun holder was observed with general buildup and mold accumulation around the outer rim and down inside. Clean and sanitize the soda gun holder as needed to eliminate buildup.
Clean and sanitize the soda gun holder and bar mounting when contamination occurs to eliminate buildup. 

Knife sharpener was observed with general buildup around the sharpening surface. Knife sharpener was taken to kitchen 3 part sink for ware washing.
Clean and sanitize the knife sharpener as needed between uses to eliminate general buildup. 

A food thermometer was observed with grease and food debris on the stem. Thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Clean and sanitize food thermometers between uses and before storage

Pizza oven had buildup of grease, carbon, and food debris on the rack and the catch tray.
Clean the pizza oven at the end of operations daily.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 All food thermometers were checked with ice water to verify accuracy after one digital thermometer appeared to be reading much higher than all the other thermometers. Digital thermometer in question was reading between 31F-32F, but two metal stem thermometers were observed reading below 30F in ice water. Thermometers were calibrated to 32°F in an ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 A lighter and writing pen were stored in a cup with food thermometers. Lighter and pen were removed from the cup. Cook was advised to cease the practice of storing other items in the cup used for thermometers. Thermometers should be clean when placed in the storage cup and need to be protected from potential contamination between uses.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Sani-bucket with a solution that smelled of bleach was located at the server area. Staff stated it was made by someone the evening prior but were unsure who made it/why it was used. The concentration of the solution was +200ppm chlorine. Manager discarded the solution during inspection.

Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use  requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. If bleach is used for wiping down tables or other surfaces used by staff and customers, follow the directions for making sanitizing solution (label is the law), and use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-803.11 Soiled, damp wiping cloth was observed in the server area by the sink. Wiping cloth had a blue discoloration, which appeared to likely be from wiping down the soda machine the evening prior. Soiled wiping cloth was placed in the proper storage area. 

Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags. Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Single service ice cream bowls were observed with food contact surface stored up in an uncovered storage container at the ice cream table.  Discussed proper storage in a clean/covered container and/or inverting bowls.

Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-201.11 One of the filters in the hood over the fryers and flat grill was observed to be damaged. Replace the damaged filter. 

Equipment and utensils shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) drip trays of cooking equipment in kitchen (carbon/food debris); 
B) bottom inside ice cream cone storage (food crumbs);
C) catch trays of conveyor oven in dining area (food crumbs);   and
D) fan covers in walkin cooler (buildup) 
Clean the aforementioned items.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Bags of open deli meat ham and turkey in the bottom of the small prep cooler had date marks of 11/7. Final day for use based on date mark was 11/13. Products were discarded in the trash during inspection.

Refrigerated foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
750.140b - Portions of chili and beef vegetable soup with date marks of 11/13 in the glass door cooler had surface temperatures at 65°F-84°F. The two chili portions were observed with internal temperatures of 91°F-94°F and 124°F. Soup had an internal temperature of 100°F. Products were made today and improperly dated. The time was not indicated on the label, but the best guesstimate as to when the cooling process began was some time between 11a and 12p per bartender's arrival time at work. Soup and chili were immediately placed back on the stove to reheat to 165°F prior to beginning the cooling process again. Cook on duty planned to utilize ice baths and/or an ice wand to speed up the cooling process. 

Cooked TCS foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Separate foods into smaller portions, use ice baths/freezers/ice wands, and stir foods frequently to aid in rapid chill process. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the required time for proper cooling.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750.120- Stem thermometers were stored in a container with writing utensils, a pair of glasses, and lighters. Some of the thermometers were not in their storage cases. All thermometers and cases were removed from container to allow for cleaning and sanitizing. Proper storage in a designated area for thermometers only was discussed.

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 - Clean spoons were observed in a tupperware storage container with handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. Proper storage with all spoon handles presented out was discussed.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Store spoons all facing one direction so that only handles will be touched when servers retrieve spoons.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
(R) 750.140 - Chili prepared earlier this morning was observed cooling in the 3 door cooler. Product was labeled with the date, but time was not written on the label. Chili had internal temperatures of 127°F. Cook noted the cooling process began around 7a when product was at a final cooking temperature of 178°F and placed in the upright freezer to begin cooling. Temperature was not being monitored over time; however, the product was still within the first two hours of cooling based on information provided. Chili was separated into two stainless steel pans and placed in the freezer uncovered to continue rapid chill. Cook was advised to stir the chili frequently and monitor the temperature to ensure food cools properly. Cook was also advised to label cooling foods with the date and time.

Cooked TCS foods shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. 
Cooling is an active process and needs to be closely monitored to ensure foods are cooling properly. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify products are reaching benchmark temperatures in the time frame designated for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs; 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4hrs (total time must not exceed 6hrs).
Educational handouts on cooling were provided.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Hamburgers and raw pork products in the bottom of the large prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures at 48°F-49°F and 47°F-48°F respectively. Products in question were in the cooler overnight and were discarded. Hamburgers just portioned with product from the 3 door cooler and apple sauce in the same prep cooler were at 45°F and 46°F. Freshly portioned hamburger and apple sauce were moved to the 3 door cooler, which was holding below 40°F. Thermometer in the large prep cooler was reading at 50°F. Manager made a call for service and adjusted the thermostat in the cooler to a colder setting. Long term storage of foods will not occur in the large prep cooler until it is able to consistently maintain products at 41°F/below. 
Technician arrived during inspection. Coils were cleaned, and additional service occurred. 

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service

750. 151 - Open container of cottage cheese in the 3 door cooler had no date mark. Product was received and opened as of the previous Friday. Product was labeled with the proper date during the inspection. 

Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS foods held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded 2/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Server salad cooler did not have a thermometer inside. A thermometer was provided during the inspection. 

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510  & 512 - Cook was observed putting on gloves without first washing hands. Handwashing prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes was discussed. Cook was then observed washing hands without proper technique. The handles of manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched without a barrier during the process. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with the cook, and a proper technique poster is on the wall next to the handsink. Cook was observed washing hands with proper technique the remainder of the inspection.

Hands shall be properly washed any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Have paper towels dispensed and ready for use to dry hands. Then use the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the facuet. If hands need to be dried further, use the soiled paper towels as a barrier to touch the handle of the dispenser to get more paper towels to finish drying hands.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Soiled salad tongs were observed inside the server salad cooler left from the prior business day. Cook removed the tongs for cleaning.

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food debris. Remove soiled equipment and utensils from service areas at the end of operations daily, and make sure items are properly cleaned and sanitized prior to using the next business day.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Cheese sauce prepared earlier this morning was observed cooling in the 3 door cooler. Product was labeled with the date, but time was not written on the label. Cheese sauce had surface and internal temperatures at 85°F and 104°F respectively. Cook noted the cooling process began by placing the product in a shallow pan in the walkin cooler, and it was around 80°F when she placed it in the covered storage container in the 3 door cooler. Based on information provided, product was still within the first two hours of cooling. Ice wand was placed in the container, and the cheese sauce was placed in the walkin cooler. Cheese sauce was observed at 50°F within the next hour.
Cooked TCS foods shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify products are reaching benchmark temperatures in the time frame designated for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs; 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4hrs (total time must not exceed 6hrs).

Portions of tartar sauce in the top of the main prep cooler were observed with surface temperatures at 52°F-55°F. Cook stated the tartar sauce was made around the time of inspector's arrival. Tartar sauce was prepared using some ingredients that started at ambient temperature. Cook was advised to monitor the temperature and verify tartar sauce reaches 41°F/below within the next 3hrs.
Reconstituted foods and foods prepared with ingredients at ambient temperature have 4hrs to reach 41°F/below once prep is completed. Label foods with date and time of prep and monitor the temperature to ensure proper cooling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 & 250 - Cheese slices in the top of the small prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 53°F and 48°F-51°F respectively. Other foods were observed at proper cold holding temperature. Cook noted the cheese in question was uncovered for a period of time, which more than likely added to elevated temperature. Cheese in question would be served or discarded by 1p.
Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service. Cover pans of food with lids between uses, and leave the tops of prep coolers closed during slow periods and between orders as much as possible to help maintain colder temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open package of cooked ham in the bottom of the small prep cooler was past the 7 day time frame for use and was improperly labeled. Label had a prep date of 3/20 and a use by date of 3/27. Ham was discarded during the inspection. Proper date marking was discussed with cook and manager. 
 Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS foods held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
NOTE: Freezing stops the clock but does not reset the 7 day time frame. Consider freezing portions of foods whenever possible to limit food waste. Just make sure to keep track of the prep date, freeze date (if different from prep date), thaw date/use by date. The total length of time for use must not exceed 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 130 - Stems of food thermometers and case were observed with stuck on food debris. Cook cleaned and sanitized thermometers and case during the inspection.
Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Use food contact surface wipes on stems before and after temperature checks, and be sure to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize the stems up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Clean and sanitize the case daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Pans of fish were stored beneath meats on a cart in the walkin cooler. Foods were arranged in proper order during the inspection so meats were on the bottom shelf of the cart and fish were stored on the upper shelves.
All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Scoop for bulk sugar was observed inside the bin with the handle down touching the product. Proper scoop storage for ready to eat foods was discussed. Scoop was positioned so the handle was up out of the sugar.
Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Basin of kitchen handsink was soiled with buildup of what appeared be food splash and some general debris. 
Handsinks and related fixtures shall be maintained clean. Clean handsinks and all related fixtures daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Taco meat in the three door cooler had a prep date of 12/5. Cook discarded the taco meat.
Container of open cottage cheese did not have a date. Product was believed to be opened earlier today. Benefit of doubt was given; product was dated and kept for use.

Refrigerated time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated and used/discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Chili in the three door cooler had a prep date of 12/12/17 and was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 65°F and 75°F respectively. Bartender noted the chili was in the process of being prepared around 9a when she arrived for work, and she observed the cook using an ice wand during the initial stages of cooling process. However, the cook that prepared the chili was gone for the day, and staff on duty were unsure as to when the cooling process began. Chili was discarded.

Cooked TCS foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hrs and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to monitor the temperature during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.512 -  Bartender was in the process of wrapping silverware and rubbed her eye. She then continued wrapping silverware. Bartender was advised on handwashing between tasks, especially after touching her face and prior to handling clean equipment. Bartender washed her hands before wrapping any more silverware.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility has bleach and quat tablets available for use. Chlorine test kits were observed, but quat test strips were not available for checking sanitizer solution. Obtain and use a quat test to verify sanitizer solutions prepared with sanitizer tablets are at proper concentration (200-400ppm per label instructions).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer solution at bar 3 part sink was observed at 100ppm quat. Solution was prepared earlier in the day and needed to be changed. Solution was remade and observed at 200ppm.

Sanitizer in kitchen 3 part sink was freshly prepared and observed at 100ppm. Three tablets were used to make the solution. Cook added more tablets to bring the solution to proper concentration of 200-400ppm quat. 
NOTE: Make sure warm water is used, per product instructions, to properly dissolve tablets.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - None of the staff working at the time of inspection had proof of a current manager certification. Afternoon cook stated he passed a class about a year ago but did not have a copy of the certificate. Facility manager arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Cook on duty at the time of inspection needs to provide a proof of certification to be maintained on-site (see general comments).

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of certified food managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling. Proof of certification must be maintained on-site.  Provide an adequate number of certified food managers and proof of certifications.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Foods in the three door cooler and small prep cooler were observed without date marks or with date marks that were beyond the 7 day time frame for use. Two bags of a cooked meat in the 3 door cooler had date marks of 7/20 & 7/27. Foods without date marks in the bottom of the small prep cooler included ham slices, an open package of deli turkey, and an open bag of pre-cooked fajita steak pieces. The two bags of meat from the 3 door cooler and the fajita steak pieces were discarded in the trash during inspection. Other foods were dated and kept for use. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dates and used or discarded within 7 days. 
NOTE: Foods that require date marking include, but are not necessarily limited to, deli meats, non-cultured dairy products (2% milk; cottage cheese), sliced tomatoes, and foods prepared in-house (gravy, cheese sauce, chili, etc.).

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Gravy observed in tabletop hot holding unit was observed with an internal temperature of 144F-150F. Cook on duty stated the temperature of the gravy was ~147F when it was placed in the hot holding well around 630-7a, and the gravy was a reheated item. The hot holding unit was not turned up hot enough to finish reheat of 165F/above w/in 2hrs. Internal temperature was checked by inspector after 9a. Gravy in question was discarded.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F/higher throughout within 2hrs. Properly reheat food to 165°F/above prior to service.
NOTE: Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify proper reheat temperature. The best practice is to have the hot holding wells on and heating while foods are reheated to 165F/above on the grill or stove. Then reheated foods are going from proper reheat temperature to hot holding and can be maintained at 135F/above after proper reheat. However, if the food is partially heated prior to being placed in the hot holding wells, make sure the equipment is on and hot enough to finish reheating foods within the remaining time for the 2hr time frame for proper reheat.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Raw beef products were observed intermixed with bags of raw fish on the top shelf of a cart in the walkin cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage with separation of raw fish from raw beef products.

All raw meat shall be properly stored. Store foods in the order of their cooking requirements with foods that have lower cooking temperatures (e.g. fish) above/separated from foods with higher cooker temperatures (e.g. beef, pork, and chicken).

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Popcorn scoop was observed by the popcorn machine and observed with grease and food crumbs on the food contact surface.
Clean and sanitize the popcorn scoop at the end of operations daily.
Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

Plastic cup was observed as a scoop inside the popping corn kernel bin. Use scoops with handles to  dispense all foods.
To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 510 - Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves after wiping hands on a damp wiping cloth used for dishes at the 3 part sink. Gloved hands were later used to turn on the 3 part sink, and gloves were not changed prior to handling cooked bacon.
Proper handwashing, when to wash hands, and proper glove use were discussed.

Hands must be properly washed prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Cloth towels (wiping cloths/dish washing rags) are prohibited for use on hands. 
Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Wash, rinse water clean, proper temperature
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - A hint of bleach was detected at the kitchen 3 part sink, and quat tablets were in use for sanitizing. The cook noted the detergent solution in the first compartment also had some bleach in it. Cook on duty was advised on proper setup of 3 part sink. Solution was emptied and remade with only detergent for the washing step of manual ware washing process.

Equipment and utensils shall be thoroughly washed in the first compartment with a hot detergent solution and kept clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The pizza oven was observed to be soiled with food debris/carbon buildup on the drip tray and the inner edge of the cooking tray by the handle. Clean the pizza oven at the end of operations daily.

Also, the currently unused table top heat/serve unit was observed with what appeared to be greasy old water in the bottom. Empty and clean the heat/serve unit. 

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 - Bloody Mary mix in the bar reach-in cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 49F and 50F respectively. Maraschino cherries had an internal temperature of 47F-48F. Both products stated  "refrigerate after opening" on labels. Cherries and bloody Mary mix were discarded in the trash. The thermometer in the cooler was observed at 50F. Manager noted the cooler in question was just serviced recently and noted it appeared the thermostat was accidentally bumped to a higher setting. Manager adjusted the thermostat, and the temperature appeared to be slowly going down. Manager was advised to refrain from storing potentially hazardous foods in the reach-in cooler until it is able to maintain a consistent temperature of 41F/below for products that require refrigeration for safety. 
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage.
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Potentially hazardous foods in the top holding area of the small prep cooler were observed at temperatures above 41F. Sliced tomatoes had surface and internal temperatures of 51F and 46F-48F respectively; while cheese slices had a surface and internal temperature of 60F. The products in question were in the top holding area of the cooler overnight, and the lid to the cooler was open while the cook was preparing breakfast orders. Cheese, sliced tomatoes, and lettuce were discarded. Cook stated smaller portions of new product would be placed in the cooler closer to lunch service. The bottom of the cooler was observed to be holding foods below 41F.
Staff were advised the top holding area of prep coolers are not necessarily intended to long-term overnight storage and to refrain from this practice unless they could verify the top area of the unit was able to maintain foods at 41F/below.
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - A plastic container of cheese sauce was observed cooling at ambient temperature on a cart next to the fryers. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 87F-88F and 114F respectively. Cheese sauce is prepared with a powder mix using water and heating on the stove. Cook noted the cheese sauce reached 200F prior to placing part of it in the steam well for service and the remaining portion in the plastic container to cool. Based on information provided the cheese sauce had ~45 minutes left in the 2hr time frame to reach 70F/below, but the time and temperature was not being tracked to know for sure. Cheese sauce was transferred to a stainless steel container and placed in an ice bath in the walkin cooler to help rapidly drop the temperature. Product had until 930a to reach an internal temperature of 70F/below. Internal temperature was observed at 75F-82F at 945a. Cheese sauce was discarded in the trash during inspection. 

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs (see general comments) Educational handout on rapid chill of cooked foods was provided.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750.820c - Sanitizer solution at bar 3 part sink was at 0ppm quat. Manager noted more water was in the sink than is typically used to make the solution. Water was emptied so the sink was a little less than half full, and one sanitizer tablet was added to the sink. The solution was then observed to be at 200ppm. All cups in the 3rd compartment were re-sanitized.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) fry baskets (grease/crumb buildup) - taken to dish area to go through ware washing;
B) soda machine ice shoot (mold along lower edge);
C) soda machine nozzles (mold where nozzles attach to machine);  and
D) hood baffles - far ends of each hood (dust/grease) - scheduled cleaning is coming up in the near future.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
Items used such as fry baskets, dry breading scoops, etc. need to be cleaned and sanitized at the end of operations daily.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - A) Men's room did not have hand soap. Provide soap at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.
A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

B) Employee restroom door was not self-closing. Adjust the door so it is self-closing.
All restrooms must have self-closing doors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250: Observed the top of the mini preparation cooler to be holding foods at 48F - 53F. Foods were probed (pickle juice 48F, cheese slices 48-53F). The kitchen is warm (96F) and this lid stayed open throughout lunch service. The base of the cooler is holding foods at 35F. The cooler was just stocked after lunch. Discussed using the four hours rule. Discard all foods not used throughout dinner service or after the four hour period has expired. Facility stocked foods around 2:00pm. Food should be used or discarded at 6:00pm. Do not store foods in the top of this cooler overnight until you can determine that the unit is able to hold foods at 41F or below.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b) Observed two covered containers of mac and cheese stored in the glass door cooler at 70F. Items did not have the time indicated on the label. Time pulled from oven was indicated on the labeling. Food was pulled at 10:30am. Foods were then placed into the walk-in cooler (which is holding temp at 29F) to rapidly cool to 41F. Foods were also left uncovered.   Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Someone has made a very nice wooded cutting board rack for the kitchen. The wood is not sealed. Seal the bare wood surface so the wood is nonabsorbent. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed a wet wiping cloth hanging off the side of the sani-bucket. Also, observed the concentration of the bucket in the kitchen to be at 0ppm Quat. The bucket was refilled with cloths being stored submerged within the bucket during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment: 750-1240  The light in the 2-door freezer is not properly shielded. Provide a light shield for this light. All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f Observed a number of items without proper labeling: swiss cheese, pepperjack cheese, cheddar cheese, ham, and chocolate milk. Label ready-to-eat, potentially hazardous foods after opening. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed turkey slices in the mini-prep fridge with a date of 5/5/16. Discarded during the inspection. See violation #2. There were a number of cheeses and meats without a proper date marking. Discussed Listeria. Keep dates clearly labeled on these foods and use within seven days.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: 750-230 The facility does not have a proper stem thermometer. Provide a stem thermometer for the kitchen staff. Educate staff on calibrating the thermometer. Make sure that thermometer is being wiped clean with a sani-cloth between uses and that at least every four hours the stem is washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The stem should read 32F when held in a slurry of ice and water (fill a cup full of ice then add water). A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d)  Observed raw chicken stored over beef in the base of the long preparation cooler. The chicken was moved to the lower shelf during the inspection. Store all raw foods in order of their cooking temperature. Chicken has the highest (165F) so it should be stored under beef, pork, and fish. Discussed cooking temperatures and related storage. All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee not properly washing hands between the preparing of foods and the cleaning of dishes. Make sure that hands are washed in-between all tasks and especially before donning gloves.  Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g Two different types of sanitizing agents are available. There are sani-tabs and liquid quat sanitizer that require the QT 10 test strips. There is also a bottle of bleach available. This sanitizing agent requires bleach test strips. Bleach test strips were supplied during the inspection. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820d Observed sanitizing contact time to be less than the required sixty seconds. Discussed in the moment and increased contact time from dipping to sixty seconds. Let washed and rinsed equipment and utensils lay in the sanitizing solution for the required amount of time.  Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed a bulk box of coffee filters to be stored underneath the drainline of the handsink in the wait area. Moved to the side during the inspection. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 Observed an electrical plate missing from the wall to the right as you enter the walk-in cooler. Provide a cover for the hole in the wall of the walk-in cooler.  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed two over the counter headache medications to be stored within condiments at the bar within one of the cabinets. The chemicals were moved to the side shelf during the inspection. Cease storing the first aide items within condiments going out to the public.  All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed an unlabeled bottle of clear liquid to not be properly labeled. The contents tested at 100ppm Cl. Labeled the bottle during the inspection. Always label clear liquid and white powders. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 The facility does not have a certified food manager present. There has been almost a complete turnover in staff. All new employees observed during today's inspection. Two employees are signed up for the MJ Kellner class next month. Also, discussed food handler cards.  All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 & 120 - A) Open packages of deli turkey and ham in the small prep cooler did not have date marks. Portioned cheeses had a prep date of 2/16, and today is the 15th. Benefit of doubt was given for deli meats. Products were labeled with a date of 2/14 and kept for use. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

B) Potentially hazardous foods (PHF) in the 3 door kitchen cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 49F-54F. All potentially hazardous foods were inventoried and discarded in the trash during the inspection (see pg 1 of Voluntary Destruction Agreement and the general comments of this report for details on foods discarded). Foods that did not have labeling to indicate refrigeration was required were placed in the walkin cooler for storage (Heinz 57 sauce; Worcestershire sauce; beef/chicken/broth bases-all stated store in cool/dry place & honey garlic rub powder). Meatloaf prepared this morning from ground beef stored in the walkin cooler was observed to have a surface temperature of 47F and was immediately placed in the oven. The 3 door cooler was not holding at proper temperature (see #4 below)

Cold PHF shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Three door cooler in the kitchen was not holding at proper temperature. A thermometer in the front was reading below 40F, but the thermometer hanging in the back was reading at 48F. Inspector's stems registered at 50F. PHF had to be discarded (see #3a part B above). Management stated they were having issues with foods freezing in the cooler, so the thermostat was adjusted to a warmer setting the other day. The thermostat was adjusted to a colder setting to see if that helped drop the temperature. In the meantime, owners contacted AirServ for service. A technician should be out later today to check the cooler and make any necessary repairs. The cooler will not be used for storage of PHF until it is able to maintain products at 41F/below. Staff were advised to call for a re-inspection once cooler is checked/repaired and functioning properly.

All refrigeration units used to store PHF shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750.130d - Pans of raw chicken were observed on the top shelf in the bottom holding area of the large prep cooler above other meats. Foods were rearranged so chicken was on the bottom shelf.

Raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom. Always store raw chicken, regardless of packaging/storage containers, below all other raw meats.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 280 - A) Cook was observed having bare hand contact with toast and shredded cheese upon arrival of inspector. Cook was advised on use of gloves/appropriate utensils for handling cooked/ready to eat foods (RTE). Cook began using gloves to handle RTE foods. 

B) Soufflé cup was observed inside onion string dipping sauce in the 3 door cooler. Sauce was discarded. Discussed use of proper utensils for dispensing foods.
 
Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use suitable utensils, such as gloves, tongs, ladles, spoons, etc., when handling/dispensing RTE foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 160 - A) Cook washed hands without proper technique. The process lasted less than 20 seconds and the handles of both the manual faucet and the paper towel dispenser were touched without a barrier. Proper technique was discussed. Cook began washing hands properly.

B) Cook was observed adjusting his clothing with gloved hands and continued with food prep without changing gloves. Proper glove use was discussed. Gloves were changed upon request of inspector.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves must be discarded/changes when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.
**Educational handouts on proper handwashing and glove use were provided**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Several lids on food storage containers were observed to be in disrepair (cracks, etc.). Replace damaged lids and other food contact surfaces as needed.

B) Surface of soda gun nozzle was observed with a few deep grooves and black buildup in the grooves. Management was advised the nozzle needs to go through manual ware washing at the bar 3 part sink, and the grooves need to be thoroughly scrubbed to see if buildup can be removed. If the buildup cannot be removed then the nozzle needs to be replaced with one that can be maintained in a clean/sanitary condition.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

C) pizza oven tray (carbon/food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

Floors and drains shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:

Maintain bleach solutions for wiping general surfaces in sani-buckets at 100-200ppm. Obtain and use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration of solutions.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f Observed bulk containers of flour and sugar to not be labeled with common name. Labeled during the inspection. Also, discussed the cooling process. When cooling, record the time that foods are removed from hot temperature. Record time and temperature to insure benchmarks are being met. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed a number of items improperly or not properly date marked in the 3-door cooler and the mini prep cooler. Baked potatoes, potato salad, marinara sauce, and milk are observed without a proper date marking (3-door cooler). And, dates in the mini prep cooler are incorrect (taco meat - 9/12, ham - 9/11, turkey - 8/28).  Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b) Bag of baked potatoes was observed in the 3-door cooler without a proper date marking or time indicated. Bag was sealed and interior held significant water accumulation. Potatoes were probed at 45F. Discussed cooling process with kitchen manager. The potatoes were discarded. The closing cook should make sure that foods are properly date marked and that the necessary cooling practices have been followed. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. Keep hot foods uncovered and in shallow pans when cooling. Make sure the time is indicated on cooling foods so that time/temperature benchmarks are met.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed thawing chicken on the counter by the handsink. Chicken was moved during the inspection. Cease allowing frozen foods to sit on counters to thaw. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 The handle of the sugar scoop was observed within the food. Scoop was repositioned to allow handle to extend out from food during the inspection. Cease storing handle within ready-to-eat foods.  Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530 Observed a personal drink without a lid nor a straw resting on a preparation counter. Store glass so that if a spill occurred, no food nor equipment would be contaminated.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-830i The three sink basins of the three-compartment sink are observed soiled with a grease line where water is usually held. Equipment should be scrubbed in first sink, dipped for a rinse in the second sink, and allowed to submerged for sixty seconds in the third sink. All dishwashing machines shall be thoroughly cleaned at least once a day or more often when necessary to maintain them in satisfactory operating condition. 750-830a All equipment and utensils placed in dish machines shall be exposed to all dishwashing cycles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The kitchen is observed in good order and clean. findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
